lines.text: Before you head on stage, you have to be fully prepared.
There is nothing more lonely than being a performer on the stage.
The blue sky is torn asunder, and the monster of iron finds us... Hmm... These lyrics aren't sticking very well.
I want to sing an aria for you one day.
Are you coming to the show today, Signor?

The goddess of victory, vengeance incarnate...
Hmm... I think I've got the lyrics down pat.
If there's nothing else, can I leave? I'd rather be preparing for my performance.
Oh, my beloved guardian, are you listening? My beloved guardian... are you listening, Signor?
I'm at the Theater. Come by any time if you want to sing.
This place is closer to the surface than the Ark. If I sing from here, will it reach the surface?
There aren't very many people at the theater, so it's a good place to practice my singing.
I will sing an aria, and you shall be my conductor.
My singing is getting more and more beautiful.
Thank you for everything you've done.
I think I can sing for a little longer.
Oh... thank you. I'll put it to good use.
Is this something a manager typically does?
Very kind of you, Signor.
I want to share the stage with you.
Your singing may not be perfect, but it inexplicably makes my heart race. How about you? Do I make your heart race?
You're the only audience I'll ever need.
I can sing any time.
Awaiting instructions.
Do I just need to go to that position?
Looks like we have some unwanted guests.
Time to sing not on stage, but on the battlefield.
It's time to sing.
The prelude to the battlefield has begun.
Hah... Again.
Da Capo.
I'll go once I fix the sound.
Signor.
The aria that won't stop until the day my life ends.
Time to bring in the chorus.
So be it.
It is finished.
Are there any more?
Ow!
Uh.
Ah, yes.
I'm sorry... I couldn't sing to the end...
The sound of the song of victory is here.
